A closed form is a great way to make a lidded jar! Here are a few helpful tips:  • poke a small hole so that as it dries and shrinks, air can release safely. • push in your flange on a straight edge, not a curve. • you don’t have to have a knob on top. This piece of functional art is here to remind you that no matter how gloopy and messy life gets, there is always love and joy bursting through. 🌈💗 I am so excited to finally start sharing the first pieces from my 2026 collection! The first half of this year has been full of learning, experimenting, and pushing my work in new directions. It has also been one of the heaviest seasons of my life. While making this collection, I found myself returning again and again to the same idea: choosing hope. This piece feels like a little celebration of that. A reminder that even when things feel overwhelming, beautiful things can still emerge from the mess. Thankfully, the scary chapter my chosen family has been living through is coming to a very happy ending, and I am sitting in deep gratitude for that. Not everyone gets that outcome, and I don’t take it for granted for a second. So tell me, what makes you stay hopeful when life feels extra gloopy? #ceramicartist #dopaminedecor #glitterinlay #rainbowart #processvideo

lidded jar tutorial - part 1 (throwing the jar body and lid)✨ have to break this up into 3 parts because it will take weeks to go through the steps (we're making these jars in real time and rely on a community studio to fire) and I simply can't fit throwing, trimming, and glazing the jars into one reel 🥲 i find 200g is perfect for throwing the small jar body, plus another 150g for the lid. you'll see i throw my jar body and lid separately, leaving a lot of the refining for the trimming stage. especially with the lids, I find it easier to throw them roughly and finesse the fit once they're leather hard. i don't wire off the lids or jars, i wait until they pop off the bats. xo shan #pottery #potterytutorial #liddedjar #handmadeceramics #canadianartist
